Primary Care Progress Note

Assessment:
Mr. Kunde is a 71-year-old male in stable condition with no acute concerns at this time.

Plan:

Radiology Report
Date: 08/28/2026
Patient: Taylor Kunde, 71-year-old male

MRI thoracolumbar spine 08/28/2026: acute osteoporotic L3 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging. Interval increase in L3 vertebral body height loss compared with radiographs from 07/07/2026. Approximately 47% loss of L3 vertebral body height. Focal kyphotic deformity at L3 measuring 24 degrees.

Impression:
The findings are consistent with an acute osteoporotic compression fracture of the L3 vertebral body. There is an interval increase in vertebral body height loss, now approximately 47%, compared to prior imaging. The focal kyphotic deformity at L3 measuring 24 degrees is noted and may have clinical significance.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/09/2026
Patient: Taylor Kunde, 71-year-old male

History:
Back pain began 07/02/2026 after bending to pick up a grandchild, 10 weeks before this visit. Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Pain NRS 5/10 despite 9 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with acetaminophen and tramadol, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has been stable to slightly improved since the fracture.

Assessment:
The patient presents with a vertebral compression fracture managed conservatively. The current pain level remains moderate but stable.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and brace use. Monitor symptoms and consider further intervention if pain worsens or functional status declines.
